last.verdict: Opendoor is buying homes far faster than it can sell them at a profit, so losses and debt are growing and the 2026 profit goal is slipping.

takeaways.label: Profit outlook worsens
takeaways.text: Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss is guided to $70–85M, versus a $31M loss in Q3. Profit per home is also expected to fall. The company says it is 'behind' its year-end profitability goal.

takeaways.label: Margins missed guidance
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 12% to $1.02B, but contribution margin was 3.3%, below the 4–4.5% guided and down from 5.8% last quarter. Net loss widened to $218M from $90M.

takeaways.label: Inventory and debt pile up
takeaways.text: Homes in inventory rose to 7,596 ($2.57B) from 5,459 last quarter. Debt tied to those homes that is due within a year jumped to $2.0B, against $910M in cash.

takeaways.label: Older homes piling up
takeaways.text: Homes listed more than 120 days rose to 18% of listed inventory from 9% last quarter. Management cites a slow market and says its focus is 'moving homes'.

history.verdict: Investors sold on a weak margin outlook despite revenue and cash-burn improvement.

reasons.label: Lower margin outlook
reasons.text: Next-quarter contribution margin guided to 4%–4.5%, below this quarter's 5.8%, blamed on seasonality.

reasons.label: Sales far below last year
reasons.text: Revenue was $883M, down about 44% from a year ago, and below analyst estimates.

reasons.label: Bigger loss, mostly stock pay
reasons.text: Net loss was $162M versus $29M a year ago, driven by about $119M of stock-based pay.
